newsitem.title: USA: CBOT, CBOE agree to margin pact for Dow products.
newsitem.headline: CBOT, CBOE agree to margin pact for Dow products.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade and Chicago Board Options Exchange have agreed to streamline margin requirements for clearing members trading equity index contracts at both exchanges, exchange officials said.

With the planned launch of derivatives products based on the Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI just a few months away, the two exchanges are developing a system to give member firms cross-margin account privileges on inter-exchange equity spreads, said CBOE Chief Executive William Brodsky.
"We have agreed with the Board of Trade that we will do this," Brodsky said in an interview.
Cross margining reduces total margin requirements for investors with a position in one equity product on one exchange and an opposite position in a similar product at another exchange.
When the market moves, losses on one position are offset by profits on the other position, resulting in less risk and therefore needing lower margins to cover that risk.
The CBOE plans an October 1 launch of DJIA options, Brodsky said. The CBOT will launch futures and futures-options on the Dow in October but has not yet set the date.
Executives at the clearinghouses for the two exchanges said they expect to have a cross-margin agreement hammered out before the Dow products begin trading.

The system would be modeled on an arrangement already in place between the CBOE and Chicago Mercantile Exchange covering inter-exchange spread positions for member firms and market professionals in S&P index contracts, said Chris Hehmeyer, chairman of the Board of Trade Clearing Corp.

"It's an explicit recognition that a long position in one product versus a short position in another product is a lower risk transaction and therefore should be margined at a lower net basis than a naked outright position at either exchange," said Todd Kerschke, equity floor manager for Cargill Investor Services Inc at the CME.
Cross margining offers significant reductions in capital requirements for maintaining inter-exchange spreads.

Mike Cahill, first vice president at the Options Clearing Corp, the common clearer for four exchanges including the CBOE, said cross-margin accounting at the OCC last year reduced member margin outlays by an average $700 million daily. "It has been a very, very successful program," he said.

The CBOT has also approached the CME in hopes of developing a cross-margin alliance for Dow/S&P index spreads and the American Stock Exchange regarding that exchange's planned DJIA unit investment trust, CBOT Chairman Patrick Arbor said.
Officials at both the CME and AMEX said separately the concept was being reviewed.
"We have taken the request under consideration, and there has been no decision made yet," said CME spokeswoman Ellen Resnick.
AMEX spokesman Dan Noonan said, "There is potential for some arrangement that would facilitate easier investing in either the futures and the equity, or the options and the equity."
